comments.text:
Fixed it. gemini told me to type this on bash:
lspci -k | grep -A 2 -E "(VGA|3D)"
then, looking at the photo of the answer from bash that I sent, told me that kernel driver in use or something was missing there. my driver was there, hardware was there, but drivers could not do the connection in between the hardware and software. so he made me use these commands in bash in a row;
sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall
sudo prime-select nvidia
sudo update-grub
and then I restarted the pc and my refresh rate was 144 instead of 60 and I could set my brightness from the battery button. though, it might not be same with yours, copy paste these to gemini and ask him help you check these maybe it helps you. love you gemini 😗
